task.title: Identify Phishing Attempts
task.shortdesc: How can you verify senders, inspect links, identify phishing red flags, and handle suspicious emails safely.

context.p: Inspecting sender addresses, links, and urgency red flags protects students, faculty, and staff from credential theft and malware. Always pause and verify suspicious messages before clicking any link or replying.

step.cmd: Verify the sender's full email address rather than trusting the display name, and contact known individuals through a separate trusted channel if a message seems unusual.
Hover your cursor over hyperlinked text—or carefully press and hold on a mobile device—to inspect the actual destination URL before clicking.
Check login page URLs before entering your Unity credentials to verify that the address starts with shib.ncsu.edu (or login.microsoftonline.com for Entra ID).
Watch for classic phishing red flags, including a false sense of urgency, unexpected messages, offers that are too good to be true, generic greetings, and typos.
Report suspicious messages via Gmail's Report phishing button, by emailing phishing@ncsu.edu, or by contacting the NC State Help Desk at 919-515-HELP (4357).
